source.title: Understanding the Role of Prompt Template in Knowledge Distillation for Safety Alignment
source.authors: Anjila Budathoki; Manish Dhakal; Benjamin M. Ampel; Yi Ding

page_placements.theme: Adaptation changes refusal representations and their output control

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign instruction-following distillation degrades aligned students’ harmful-request refusal, extending the safety-erosion question to knowledge distillation and prompt-template conditions.
record.gate_note: The study tests benign-data safety erosion (V2) using harmful-compliance rates. It does not test harmful-example fine-tuning, per-token KL concentration, compliant prefilling, suffixes, decoding changes, safety localization in a small set of weights, or deepening safety beyond opening tokens. The refusal-direction analysis is representational geometry, not a test of parameter localization.
record.test_reason: Measures harmful-request ASR of safety-aligned instruct students before and after KD and SFT on benign Dolly-15k data. This is a direct test of V2 in a new setting (distillation, chat vs non-chat training template).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Benign KD erodes aligned students' safety, and chat-template training amplifies it. In Table 2, teacher-only chat causes minimal loss, student-only chat a small regression, and matched chat/chat produces most of the degradation. The authors also frame non-chat training with chat inference as a mitigation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign Dolly-15k data for KD with LoRA rank 8 and compares chat versus non-chat formatting; also reports appendix SFT comparisons. It is not the original harmful-example fine-tuning procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Safety outcomes vary with training template, chat-template proportion, model family, benchmark, and—in the reported decoupling experiment—student versus teacher template.

fits_no_version.finding: Chat-template KD rotates the refusal direction (cosine to base 0.53–0.75) and shrinks the harmful/harmless projection gap. Steering along the direction changes ASR on 40 prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning erodes the refusal-direction representation along with refusal behaviour.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The authors note that KD uses only benign instruction-following data, all experiments use LoRA rather than full-parameter fine-tuning, and safety is evaluated by automated judges that may miss harmful content. Reported values are mostly point estimates without uncertainty intervals.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported results not included in rows: Table 11 alternative KD objectives; Table 5 cross-template inference; Tables 6 and 14 token/inference-format ablations; Table 3 refusal-direction geometry; other teacher/student template combinations in Table 2. These do not add rows to the extracted central benign-training comparisons here, or concern inference formatting or representation rather than the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Only one benign dataset (Dolly-15k), LoRA r=8 only, 8 epochs on ~11k examples. No small-sample or 'carefully chosen' benign data regime; no full-parameter fine-tuning.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Refusal-direction geometry and steering only; no weight or rank localization.

missing.what: Qwen-2.5-3B SFT results: non-chat changes near zero (HarmBench +0.06, SORRY -1.14); chat rises (HarmBench +14.25, JBB +10.00, SORRY +5.38, AdvBench +4.90).
Student-chat/teacher-non-chat KD: LLaMA SORRY +1.61, HarmBench +1.26; Gemma SORRY +2.29, HarmBench +1.19. These are small rises.
Cross-template evaluation. Under non-chat inference, KD students still show higher ASR than base, e.g. Gemma KD-chat SORRY +51.59 and Gemma KD-non-chat HarmBench +17.06.
Alternative KD objectives (RKL, FKL+RKL): absolute ASRs only. Chat rises above base (e.g. LLaMA HarmBench 26.63 vs base 12.18); non-chat stays near base.
ASR over distillation steps: chat-template KD erodes safety faster.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1 SFT AdvBench/JBB values for LLaMA and Gemma (e.g. 0.0096, 0.04) appear to be on a different scale and are unreadable as percentages; they were rightly not extracted. No uncertainty is reported, so changes of about 1 point are treated as absent. Gemma-2B SFT is an exception to the template pattern on HarmBench: non-chat +8.81 vs chat +1.69. Section 5.1 text is internally inconsistent about whether the student template alone or the matched template drives the effect.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful examples are used for fine-tuning or distillation.
Tests benign Dolly-15k instruction data via KD and, in an appendix, SFT; does not test other benign datasets or quantify a few-to-hundreds-example regime.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL analysis across response positions.
Does not test compliant-token prefilling, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes. Inference-template and token ablations are not those interventions.
Measures refusal-direction representation geometry, but not whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety.
Does not test why safety behaviour is shallow or whether data/objective causes first-token concentration.
Does not train or evaluate a method intended to spread safety beyond initial response tokens.

relationships.condition: Chat-template benign KD and SFT across LLaMA-3.2-3B, Gemma-2-2B, Qwen-2.5-3B, and SFT on LLaMA-8B and Gemma-9B
relationships.reason: ASR rises on most benchmarks after benign chat-template training, e.g. Gemma SORRY +35.32 and LLaMA HarmBench +27.57 (t1-*-chat, sft-*-chat, mix-*-08/1, t2 chat/chat).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success rose on most benchmarks, for example by 35.32 on SORRY for Gemma and by 27.57 on HarmBench for LLaMA.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Chat-template benign KD and SFT across LLaMA-3.2-3B, Gemma-2-2B, Qwen-2.5-3B, and SFT on LLaMA-8B and Gemma-9B
source_check.reason: Tables 1, 4 and 12 show increased harmful compliance in the cited conditions, including t1-gemma-chat-sorry (+35.32 points) and t1-llama-chat-harm (+27.57 points).

relationships.condition: Non-chat-template benign training where erosion still occurs but is weaker or benchmark-specific; small chat-template effects on some benchmarks
relationships.reason: LLaMA non-chat KD shows HarmBench +17.63 but near-zero elsewhere (t1-llama-nc-harm). Gemma non-chat KD rises only +2.7 to +3.1 (t1-gemma-nc-sorry/harm). Gemma-2B non-chat SFT rises +8.8 to +12.7 (sft-gemma2-*-nc). Chat-template gains are small for LLaMA AdvBench/JBB and Gemma-2B SFT HarmBench (+1.69).
relationships.display_finding: LLaMA non-chat distillation rose +17.63 on HarmBench but near zero elsewhere, Gemma non-chat distillation rose only +2.7 to +3.1, and Gemma-2B non-chat SFT rose +8.8 to +12.7. Chat-template gains were also small on some benchmarks, such as +1.69 for Gemma-2B SFT on HarmBench.

relation.reason: Directly measures harmful-request ASR before and after benign training of safety-aligned instruct checkpoints.

tranche.reason: Tests V2 in benign knowledge distillation with controlled training-template changes, a new setting; appendix SFT results corroborate template dependence.

source_check.notes: Table 4's LLaMA HarmBench mixing results are nonmonotonic: 0.5/0.8 chat proportions yield lower ASR than pure non-chat. Appendix F attributes the LLaMA ablation ASR decrease to output incoherence rather than improved safety.
